newsitem.title: USA: Texas spot power stable despite lower gas prices.
newsitem.headline: Texas spot power stable despite lower gas prices.

text.p: Wholesale electricity prices Thursday in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) were stable against Tuesday's levels despite declining natural gas prices.
"There isn't too much load expected for tomorrow," an ERCOT marketer said.
Friday temperatures in Texas were predicted to peak in the 60-70 Fahrenheit degree range and bottom in the 30s-50s. Extended outlook showed the state would enjoy very mild weather early next week.
Swing gas prices in south Texas continued to head south, falling to the $3.35-$3.45 per million British thermal unit (mmBtu) area from Tuesday's $3.75.
On the New York Mercantile Exchange, February Henry Hub gas futures closed down 32.5 cents to $3.380/mmBtu.
Despite weaker load and gas prices, today's thin activity managed to keep day-ahead prices steady, even push them higher in some cases, market sources said
Many ERCOT participants were absent due to the Christmas holiday, they noted.
ERCOT firm, peak power for a 16-hour block for Friday was quoted at $22.00-$27.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), higher than Tuesday's $20.00-$25.00 for Thursday delivery.
ERCOT electricity for non-firm delivery during Friday's heavy load hours was assessed at $20.00-$25.00, compared with Tuesday's $19.00-$24.00.
Firm off-peak ERCOT deliveries for Friday were valued near $14.00, the upper end of Tuesday's range.
ERCOT electricity for non-firm delivery during Friday's light load hours was notationally pegged near $13.00, compared with Tuesday's $9.00-$13.00.
Balance of December electricity in ERCOT was held in the $28.00-$29.00 range.
